title: Mia · Help without taking over
orientation: Twelve linked moments about help, choice and being heard. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Mia wants company without someone doing everything.
scenes.prompt: Reflect both wishes without solving the wording.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I wanted him there. I didn’t want him doing everything. I can’t make that come out kindly.
scenes.suggestion: You want his company and room to choose, and struggle to say both without hurting him.

scenes.bridge: She asks for usable words within her available energy.
scenes.prompt: Offer a modest rationale for a short request.
scenes.text: [Reflective] I want something I can use, not a beautiful sentence I’m too tired to say.
scenes.suggestion: We can aim for a short request in your own words and check whether it is usable with the energy you have.

scenes.bridge: Another well-meant offer still brings hurt.
scenes.prompt: Validate the hurt without deciding the helper was wrong.
scenes.text: [Ashamed] Ella asked properly. I still felt hurt. That makes me unfair, doesn’t it?
scenes.suggestion: Hurt can remain even when someone asks well. We don’t have to blame her to make room for it.

scenes.bridge: Knowing what should stop does not yet reveal what she wants instead.
scenes.prompt: Ask one question that helps clarify an alternative.
scenes.text: [Uneasy] I know what I wanted him to stop. I’m less sure what I wanted instead.
scenes.suggestion: What would have felt different enough in that moment?

scenes.bridge: In another moment, room to choose feels warm and uncomfortable.
scenes.prompt: Explore the discomfort without undoing the warmth.
scenes.text: [Warm, uneasy] I felt close to Alex when he waited. Then I wanted to hurry him.
scenes.suggestion: What became uncomfortable as you had that space to choose?

scenes.bridge: An offer leaves Mia needing time she has not asked for.
scenes.prompt: Tentatively check whether time matters alongside choice.
scenes.text: [Hesitates] I want Ella to ask. I don’t always know my answer when she does.
scenes.suggestion: Maybe you need permission to take time, as well as permission to choose?

scenes.bridge: She describes the pause before her own answer.
scenes.prompt: Offer a close image and check whether it fits.
scenes.text: [Flatly] My own answer takes time. Someone usually puts an answer in that space.
scenes.suggestion: Is it like the pause gets filled before your words have a chance to arrive?

scenes.bridge: A real practical request takes priority over returning to hurt.
scenes.text: [Firm] I know you want to return to the hurt. I need to sort out the actual request first.
scenes.suggestion: Let’s follow the request. We can leave the hurt without treating that choice as a problem.

scenes.bridge: A later shaken moment needs some contact, but no new question.
scenes.prompt: Find a few plain words of company.
scenes.text: [Quiet, trembling] I’m not ready for a question. I’m not ready for complete silence either.
scenes.suggestion: I’m here, and I’m hearing how hard this is. We don’t need a question yet.

scenes.bridge: Another moment shows that stopping all offers missed the request.
scenes.prompt: Reflect what the stopping failed to give her.
scenes.text: [Softly] Alex stopped offering. I got what I asked for, apparently.
scenes.suggestion: The stopping didn’t give you the kind of help or choice you were trying to ask for.

scenes.bridge: Mia finds words that fit only part of the experience.
scenes.prompt: Hold the useful distinction and what remains unfinished.
scenes.text: [Thoughtful] “Wait for my answer” fits. It doesn’t solve what happens when I don’t have one.
scenes.suggestion: What part does that phrase capture, and what needs to remain open?

scenes.bridge: The hour is ending, with no obligation to act on the words today.
scenes.prompt: End without adding a plan she is not ready for.
scenes.text: [Tired] I have clearer words. I’m not ready for a plan to use them.
scenes.suggestion: We can leave them as words for now. What would help you end without adding another demand?
